document: The marathon cohort: the names-free records every marathon analysis and every recount reads (format: analysis/cohort.py; readers: analysis/cohort.py and scripts/lib/cohort.cjs). An output stores the SHA-256 of this file’s exact bytes to say which cohort it was built on.

rule.editions: an edition has a file when the edition policy counts it or leaves it an own-record view (`use`: counted or own_record); every other edition with written records gives recorded times only and is listed in `other_editions` with its raw count, the policy’s category and the release’s tier, weaker-source mark and split tier, so the manifest indexes every written edition with its tier
rule.records: a file holds every written record of its edition: those that pass the timing checks with id, runner, sex, age and nine times (in a counted edition they are the counted records, in an own-record edition the own-record records), and every other one with its id, the reason its timing is not usable and its nine times when all nine parse
rule.not_held: records of editions that give recorded times only: no pooled split analysis may use them. The linked-records family reads their finish times from the adapted input (the editions of its universe F, adoption decision D22); a reader that needs their number reads `other_editions`
rule.series: `series` on an edition row is the race of a plain key that holds several, from the race registry’s reviewed series note (Warsaw: Orlen Warsaw Marathon 2015 to 2018, PZU Warsaw Marathon 2019 to 2026; adoption ruling D29); null elsewhere. No existing builder groups by it
rule.race_date: every counted edition has a race date (`race_date_source`: the weather row, a reviewed date from the producer’s note, or a reviewed date from a cited external source, adoption ruling D27); the builder stops otherwise
rule.runner: the runner of a record is the smallest record id among the written marathon records of its runner key in the identity file (analysis/build_identity.py: a link of a keyed tier whose person passes the three screens over both distances); a record without a key has none. No name, bib or person id is written
rule.link: a record with a runner carries the class of its link: h when the link’s tier in the producer’s build is high_elite or high, m when it is medium (adoption ruling D38). A reading on high links alone follows each runner over its records of class h only; `linkage.high_links` counts the counted records on that basis
rule.times: the nine cumulative times in seconds as analysis/build_pacing.py prepare() parses them, exactly

linkage.identity_rule: analysis/build_identity.py (links of a keyed tier whose person passes the three screens, over both distances)
